## Power of court to control evidence

## 32.1

[PART 32 – EVIDENCE > 32.1] (1) The court may control the evidence by giving directions as to –

[PART 32 – EVIDENCE > 32.1] (a) the issues on which it requires evidence;

[PART 32 – EVIDENCE > 32.1] (b) the nature of the evidence which it requires to decide those issues; and

[PART 32 – EVIDENCE > 32.1] (c) the way in which the evidence is to be placed before the court.

[PART 32 – EVIDENCE > 32.1] (2) The court may use its power under this rule to exclude evidence that would otherwise be admissible.

[PART 32 – EVIDENCE > 32.1] (3) The court may limit cross-examination (GL) .

## Evidence of witnesses – general rule

## 32.2

[PART 32 – EVIDENCE > 32.2] (1) The general rule is that any fact which needs to be proved by the evidence of witnesses is to be proved –

[PART 32 – EVIDENCE > 32.2] (a) at trial, by their oral evidence given in public; and

[PART 32 – EVIDENCE > 32.2] (b) at any other hearing, by their evidence in writing.

[PART 32 – EVIDENCE > 32.2] (2) This is subject –

[PART 32 – EVIDENCE > 32.2] (a) to any provision to the contrary contained in these Rules or elsewhere; or

[PART 32 – EVIDENCE > 32.2] (b) to any order of the court.

[PART 32 – EVIDENCE > 32.2] (3) The court may give directions –

[PART 32 – EVIDENCE > 32.2] (a) identifying or limiting the issues to which factual evidence may be directed;

[PART 32 – EVIDENCE > 32.2] (b) identifying the witnesses who may be called or whose evidence may be read; or

[PART 32 – EVIDENCE > 32.2] (c) limiting the length or format of witness statements.

## Evidence by video link or other means

## 32.3 The court may allow a witness to give evidence through a video link or by other means.

## Requirement to serve witness statements for use at trial

## 32.4

[PART 32 – EVIDENCE > 32.4] (1) A witness statement is a written statement signed by a person which contains the evidence which that person would be allowed to give orally.

[PART 32 – EVIDENCE > 32.4] (2) The court will order a party to serve on the other parties any witness statement of the oral evidence which the party serving the statement intends to rely on in relation to any issues of fact to be decided at the trial.

[PART 32 – EVIDENCE > 32.4] (3) The court may give directions as to –

[PART 32 – EVIDENCE > 32.4] (a) the order in which witness statements are to be served; and

[PART 32 – EVIDENCE > 32.4] (b) whether or not the witness statements are to be filed.

## Use at trial of witness statements which have been served

## 32.5

[PART 32 – EVIDENCE > 32.5] (1) If –

[PART 32 – EVIDENCE > 32.5] (a) a party has served a witness statement; and

[PART 32 – EVIDENCE > 32.5] (b) he wishes to rely at trial on the evidence of the witness who made the statement,

[PART 32 – EVIDENCE > 32.5] he must call the witness to give oral evidence unless the court orders otherwise or he puts the statement in as hearsay evidence.

[PART 32 – EVIDENCE > 32.5] (Part 33 contains provisions about hearsay evidence)

[PART 32 – EVIDENCE > 32.5] (2) Where a witness is called to give oral evidence under paragraph (1), his witness statement shall stand as his evidence in chief (GL) unless the court orders otherwise.

[PART 32 – EVIDENCE > 32.5] (3) A witness giving oral evidence at trial may with the permission of the court –

[PART 32 – EVIDENCE > 32.5] (a) amplify his witness statement; and

[PART 32 – EVIDENCE > 32.5] (b) give evidence in relation to new matters which have arisen since the witness statement was served on the other parties.

[PART 32 – EVIDENCE > 32.5] (4) The court will give permission under paragraph (3) only if it considers that there is good reason not to confine the evidence of the witness to the contents of his witness statement.

[PART 32 – EVIDENCE > 32.5] (5) If a party who has served a witness statement does not–

[PART 32 – EVIDENCE > 32.5] (a) call the witness to give evidence at trial; or

[PART 32 – EVIDENCE > 32.5] (b) put the witness statement in as hearsay evidence, any other party may put the witness statement in as hearsay evidence.

## Evidence in proceedings other than at trial

## 32.6

[PART 32 – EVIDENCE > 32.6] (1) Subject to paragraph (2), the general rule is that evidence at hearings other than the trial is to be by witness statement unless the court, a practice direction or any other enactment requires otherwise.

[PART 32 – EVIDENCE > 32.6] (2) At hearings other than the trial, a party may, rely on the matters set out in –

[PART 32 – EVIDENCE > 32.6] (a) his statement of case; or

[PART 32 – EVIDENCE > 32.6] (b) his application notice, if the statement of case or application notice is verified by a statement of truth.

## Order for cross-examination

## 32.7

[PART 32 – EVIDENCE > 32.7] (1) Where, at a hearing other than the trial, evidence is given in writing, any party may apply to the court for permission to cross-examine the person giving the evidence.

[PART 32 – EVIDENCE > 32.7] (2) If the court gives permission under paragraph (1) but the person in question does not attend as required by the order, his evidence may not be used unless the court gives permission.

## Form of witness statement

## 32.8 A witness statement must comply with the requirements set out in Practice Direction 32.

[PART 32 – EVIDENCE > 32.8 A witness statement must comply with the requirements set out in Practice Direction 32.] (Part 22 requires a witness statement to be verified by a statement of truth)

## Witness summaries

## 32.9

[PART 32 – EVIDENCE > 32.9] (1) A party who –

[PART 32 – EVIDENCE > 32.9] (a) is required to serve a witness statement for use at trial; but

[PART 32 – EVIDENCE > 32.9] (b) is unable to obtain one, may apply, without notice, for permission to serve a witness summary instead.

[PART 32 – EVIDENCE > 32.9] (2) A witness summary is a summary of –

[PART 32 – EVIDENCE > 32.9] (a) the evidence, if known, which would otherwise be included in a witness statement; or

[PART 32 – EVIDENCE > 32.9] (b) if the evidence is not known, the matters about which the party serving the witness summary proposes to question the witness.

[PART 32 – EVIDENCE > 32.9] (3) Unless the court orders otherwise, a witness summary must include the name and address of the intended witness.

[PART 32 – EVIDENCE > 32.9] (4) Unless the court orders otherwise, a witness summary must be served within the period in which a witness statement would have had to be served.

[PART 32 – EVIDENCE > 32.9] (5) Where a party serves a witness summary, so far as practicable rules 32.4 (requirement to serve witness statements for use at trial), 32.5(3) (amplifying witness statements), and 32.8 (form of witness statement) shall apply to the summary.

## Consequence of failure to serve witness statement or summary

[PART 32 – EVIDENCE > Consequence of failure to serve witness statement or summary] 32.10 If a witness statement or a witness summary for use at trial is not served in respect of an intended witness within the time specified by the court, then the witness may not be called to give oral evidence unless the court gives permission.

## Cross-examination on a witness statement

[PART 32 – EVIDENCE > Cross-examination on a witness statement] 32.11 Where a witness is called to give evidence at trial, he may be cross-examined on his witness statement whether or not the statement or any part of it was referred to during the witness’s evidence in chief (GL) .

## Use of witness statements for other purposes

## 32.12

[PART 32 – EVIDENCE > 32.12] (1) Except as provided by this rule, a witness statement may be used only for the purpose of the proceedings in which it is served.

[PART 32 – EVIDENCE > 32.12] (2) Paragraph (1) does not apply if and to the extent that–

[PART 32 – EVIDENCE > 32.12] (a) the witness gives consent in writing to some other use of it;

[PART 32 – EVIDENCE > 32.12] (b) the court gives permission for some other use; or

[PART 32 – EVIDENCE > 32.12] (c) the witness statement has been put in evidence at a hearing held in public.

[PART 32 – EVIDENCE > 32.12] (3) This rule applies to affidavits in the same way as it applies to witness statements.

## Availability of witness statements for inspection

## 32.13

[PART 32 – EVIDENCE > 32.13] (1) A witness statement which stands as evidence in chief (GL) is open to inspection during the course of the trial unless the court otherwise directs.

[PART 32 – EVIDENCE > 32.13] (2) Any person may ask for a direction that a witness statement is not open to inspection.

[PART 32 – EVIDENCE > 32.13] (3) The court will not make a direction under paragraph (2) unless it is satisfied that a witness statement should not be open to inspection because of –

[PART 32 – EVIDENCE > 32.13] (a) the interests of justice;

[PART 32 – EVIDENCE > 32.13] (b) the public interest;

[PART 32 – EVIDENCE > 32.13] (c) the nature of any expert medical evidence in the statement;

[PART 32 – EVIDENCE > 32.13] (d) the nature of any confidential information (including information relating to personal financial matters) in the statement; or

[PART 32 – EVIDENCE > 32.13] (e) the need to protect the interests of any child or protected party.

[PART 32 – EVIDENCE > 32.13] (4) The court may exclude from inspection words or passages in the statement.

## False statements

## 32.14

[PART 32 – EVIDENCE > 32.14] Proceedings for contempt of court may be brought against a person who makes or causes to be made a false statement in a document, prepared in anticipation of or during proceedings and verified by a statement of truth, without an honest belief in its truth.

[PART 32 – EVIDENCE > 32.14] (Part 22 makes provision for statements of truth.)

[PART 32 – EVIDENCE > 32.14] (Part 81 contains provisions in relation to proceedings for contempt of court.)

## Affidavit evidence

## 32.15

[PART 32 – EVIDENCE > 32.15] (1) Evidence must be given by affidavit (GL) instead of or in addition to a witness statement if this is required by the court, a provision contained in any other rule, a practice direction or any other enactment.

[PART 32 – EVIDENCE > 32.15] (2) Nothing in these Rules prevents a witness giving evidence by affidavit at a hearing other than the trial if he chooses to do so in a case where paragraph (1) does not apply, but the party putting forward the affidavit may not recover the additional cost of making it from any other party unless the court orders otherwise.

[PART 32 – EVIDENCE > 32.15] (Rule 32.12 makes provision about the use of affidavits for purposes other than the proceedings in which they are served.)

## Form of affidavit

## 32.16 An affidavit (GL) must comply with the requirements set out in Practice Direction 32.

## Affidavit made outside the jurisdiction

## 32.17 A person may make an affidavit (GL) outside the jurisdiction in accordance with –

[PART 32 – EVIDENCE > 32.17 A person may make an affidavit (GL) outside the jurisdiction in accordance with –] (a) this Part; or

[PART 32 – EVIDENCE > 32.17 A person may make an affidavit (GL) outside the jurisdiction in accordance with –] (b) the law of the place where he makes the affidavit.

## Notice to admit facts

## 32.18

[PART 32 – EVIDENCE > 32.18] (1) A party may serve notice on another party requiring him to admit the facts, or the part of the case of the serving party, specified in the notice.

[PART 32 – EVIDENCE > 32.18] (2) A notice to admit facts must be served no later than 21 days before the trial.

[PART 32 – EVIDENCE > 32.18] (3) Where the other party makes any admission in response to the notice, the admission may be used against him only –

[PART 32 – EVIDENCE > 32.18] (a) in the proceedings in which the notice to admit is served; and

[PART 32 – EVIDENCE > 32.18] (b) by the party who served the notice.

[PART 32 – EVIDENCE > 32.18] (4) The court may allow a party to amend or withdraw any admission made by him on such terms as it thinks just.

## Notice to admit or produce documents

## 32.19

[PART 32 – EVIDENCE > 32.19] (1) A party shall be deemed to admit the authenticity of a document disclosed to him under Part 31 (disclosure and inspection of documents) unless he serves notice that he wishes the document to be proved at trial.

[PART 32 – EVIDENCE > 32.19] (2) A notice to prove a document must be served –

[PART 32 – EVIDENCE > 32.19] (a) by the latest date for serving witness statements; or

[PART 32 – EVIDENCE > 32.19] (b) within 7 days of disclosure of the document, whichever is later.

## Notarial acts and instruments

[PART 32 – EVIDENCE > Notarial acts and instruments] 32.20 A notarial act or instrument may be received in evidence without further proof as duly authenticated in accordance with the requirements of law unless the contrary is proved.
